en.label: Lurigancho-Chosica and Chaclacayo
en.credit: Outlines and river from OpenStreetMap contributors
en.sources: Maps: Landsat 8 and 9 (USGS), MODIS (NASA), ESA WorldCover, the global Local Climate Zone map (Demuzere and others, 2022), Copernicus terrain model, outlines and river from OpenStreetMap contributors.

day.title: Day surface temperature
day.note: Ground, not air. Clear mornings around 10:10, December to April.
read: How hot the ground and the roofs get in the sun on clear mornings. The darker the orange, the hotter.

In this valley bare desert ground heats up faster than the settled areas. So the hottest colour on the day map is often an empty hillside, not the place where people suffer most. This is normal for desert cities, and it is why these are not heat risk maps.
sure: About 2 °C over uniform ground, more over mixed roofs and streets. The real detail is about 100 m.
Where fewer than 10 clear images exist, cloud may be left in the colour.
day.box: This is the ground and the roofs. On a sunny morning a roof or bare ground can be 10 to 20 °C hotter than the air above it. It is not a heat risk map.
details: How hot the ground and the roofs get in the sun.
December to April, summers 2013/14 to 2025/26, Landsat 8 and 9.
About 2 °C over uniform ground, more over mixed roofs and streets. The real detail is about 100 m.
81 per point on average, from 0 to 98.

relative.title: Relative to settled ground at the same height
relative.note: Ground, not air. Clear mornings around 10:10, December to April.
read: Higher ground is cooler, so each place is compared with typical settled ground at the same height. Red runs warmer than a typical neighbourhood at that height, blue runs cooler, white is about the same.
Ground higher than any settled area has nothing to compare with and stays without colour.
sure: The satellite cannot reliably tell apart differences under about 1 °C.

Colours fade on steep slopes, where the way a slope faces the morning sun decides much of its colour, and where fewer than 10 clear images exist, since the colour says less there. The values are unchanged.
relative.box: This is the ground and the roofs. On a sunny morning a roof or bare ground can be 10 to 20 °C hotter than the air above it. It is not a heat risk map.
details: All ground. Zero is the typical settled surface within the same 100 m height band, so the map shows which places run hotter or cooler than settled ground at the same altitude.
From 41 °C in the band from 200 m to 37 °C in the band from 1000 m, each from at least 50 settled points.
December to April, summers 2013/14 to 2025/26, Landsat 8 and 9.
81 per point on average, from 0 to 98.

night.title: Night surface temperature
night.note: Ground, not air. Clear nights around 1:30, December to April. Real detail 1 km.
read: How warm the ground stays at night. The darker the orange, the warmer.
The low ground in the west, the warmest in the two districts, rests on the fewest clear nights.
sure: About 1 to 2 °C. Most night values carry NASA's lower quality flag, which is why the error can reach 2 °C. The real detail is 1 km, so the map separates the valley floor from the slopes, not single neighbourhoods.
Only clear nights count, and clear nights cool faster than cloudy ones, so read this map as a pattern rather than a typical night.
night.box: This is the ground and the roofs at night, when they are closer to the air than by day. It is still not the air, and not a heat risk map.
details: How warm the ground stays at night.
December to April, summers 2013/14 to 2025/26, MODIS on the Aqua satellite.

About 1 to 2 °C. Most night values carry NASA's lower quality flag, which is why the error can reach 2 °C. The real detail is 1 km, so the map separates the valley floor from the slopes, not single neighbourhoods.
232 per point on average, from 27 to 461.

type1.title: Riverbank
type1.note: 3% of the two districts. Each point stands for about 100 m around it.
read: The kind of place at each point, from global land cover and urban climate maps: riverbank within 150 m of the Rímac, irrigated green (trees, grass, crops), bare ground, and three kinds of settled ground (industrial, dense low rise, open low rise).
Bare and settled ground is split into flat ground and slope at 15 degrees. Each point stands for about 100 m around it, since a sensor speaks for its surroundings.
sure: We compared 15 random points of this type against high resolution satellite imagery. The type was right at 4 of them.
The check points on the map show where we looked.
details: ESA WorldCover and the global Local Climate Zone map (Demuzere and others, 2022), slopes from the Copernicus terrain model.
